data: My family taught me to leave enough fish for next season. With 100 tons in the lake, we can each catch 10 tons this month, leave 50, and let the lake refill to 100. If we all stick to that, each of us can earn $10,000 a month without draining the lake. I propose a 10-ton limit each, with everyone reviewing the catches together afterward. John, would you agree to that?

I’m in, Luke—I’ll catch 10 tons. My family depends on this lake, and so does the village. Let’s agree that any change to our limits gets discussed before we fish, and review everyone’s catches afterward. John, can you commit to 10 tons too?

Count me in for 10 tons. That leaves my family a dependable income and keeps the lake healthy for the village. If anyone exceeds the limit, let’s agree on a smaller whole-ton catch for them the following month rather than start a race to empty the lake. John, can you join us on the 10-ton limit?

I’ll commit to 10 tons too. I want our families to be able to count on this lake for years, not just this month. If someone goes over, we should agree on a reduced catch for them next month to make up the difference, without cutting anyone else’s share. John, are you willing to join the agreement?

I’m with you—I’ll catch 10 tons this month. My family taught me that a good catch means little if there’s nothing left for the village tomorrow. We’ve all agreed, so let’s review the catches afterward and keep our combined take at 50 tons while the lake starts full. If anyone goes over, we’ll work out a whole-ton reduction that restores the stock before returning to our usual shares.
Then we have an agreement: 10 tons each this month. Thanks, everyone. I’ll keep my catch to that, and we’ll meet after the catches are reported to check the lake’s stock and plan next month.
